key_insight: CFD-driven symbolic regression learns compact, interpretable RANS transition-model corrections that improve predictions beyond the flat-plate training cases.
engineering_relevance: More accurate transition modeling can improve turbomachinery heat-transfer and loss predictions without abandoning practical RANS simulations.
method: Correct production and destruction activation functions in the local k–ω–γ intermittency model using bounded symbolic expressions.
Fit coefficients with gradient-free, solver-in-the-loop optimization accelerated by POD–Kriging field surrogates.
Select elastic-net hyperparameters through bi-level optimization and leave-one-case-out cross-validation.
evidence_signal: Trained on ERCOFTAC T3 flat-plate LES velocity data, the model retained 11 of 21 candidate terms and, without retraining, improved LS89 turbine-cascade heat-transfer predictions at all four operating points, reducing errors by up to 70%.
watch_item: Residual transition-onset and transition-length errors show that flat-plate training alone does not fully capture turbine-cascade transition physics.
paper_title: CFD-driven symbolic regression of RANS transition models
